page: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance features an Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor clocked at up to 4.2 GHz, configured with 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs via dedicated hyperthreading. The CPU includes 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and vector instruction extensions including AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8. It is allocated 192.0 GB of memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage includes 2832 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD space with support for Premium Storage tiers. No discrete GPUs are provided.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent high-tier throughput across multi-core compute and data-intensive tasks. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 2,140.0 and a multi-core score of 19,924.0, complemented by a PassMark CPU score of 62,410.33. Memory subsystem benchmarks show high un-cached memory bandwidth, registering 232.42 GB/sec for large-block reads and 100.8 GB/sec for large-block writes. Highly parallel decompression via bzip3 reached 302.92 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput reached 80.58 GB/sec. In-memory data access performs strongly, demonstrated by 67.91 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a PassMark database score of 25,573.3. CPU-based machine learning inference runs effectively via AMX and vector extensions, delivering 342.39 tokens per second on text generation using a small 135M model and 31.29 tokens per second on a 7B model.

The inclusion of 2832 GB of local NVMe SSD storage offers low-latency scratch space without relying entirely on remote network-attached disks, aiding qualitative cost efficiency for IOPS-heavy operations. The server does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which may require separate networking allocation depending on deployment architecture. The hardware configuration makes the D48ds_v6 well suited for enterprise database hosting, distributed caching clusters, large software compilation pipelines, web serving at scale, and CPU-driven inference pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 48 vCPUs (24 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running up to 4.2 GHz. The system provides 192.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and integrates 2832 GB of local NVMe SSD storage with Premium Storage capabilities. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-quartile performance across Geekbench multi-core (19,924.0), PassMark CPU (62,410.33), and uncached memory bandwidth operations. Hardware-level acceleration features such as AVX-512 and AMX instructions drive strong performance in cryptographic tasks, database operations, and CPU-based LLM inference. Lacking a discrete GPU, this instance is structured for high-throughput enterprise databases, in-memory caches such as Redis, large-scale continuous integration or software compilation workloads, and intensive web tier hosting.
